The subject is locked (the product shape/angle/orientation are completely fixed, but material rendering is re-evaluated for physical accuracy), and the scene environment is replaced; the new scene rigidly adapts the perspective around the subject: the contact points are precisely aligned, and the perspective vanishing point is consistent. Material properties are realistically re-rendered: for transparent or semi-transparent objects, opaque artifacts are removed to restore full transparency, allowing the new background to be visible with physically correct refraction and distortion. The light and shadow logic is deeply unified: the light source direction/color/intensity are completely matched with the new scene, shadows are cast onto the new ground, and reflections accurately map the new environment. If the subject emits light, it acts as a local light source, casting a realistic glow on the surroundings. The edges are seamlessly connected at the pixel level, eliminating splicing marks and achieving a physically realistic fusion of perspective/light/material.
